## 1. The question, frozen

By its title and its opening promise, this document answers one question: **how was "The Raven" composed?** Poe sharpens it himself — the design is to show "that no one point in its composition is referrible either to accident or intuition" and that the work "proceeded, step by step... with the precision and rigid consequence of a mathematical problem." Range: this one poem, with the method offered as general. Kind: a claimed forward account of how a thing was made, plus a design rationale for each choice. He sets one limit out loud — the "circumstance or necessity" that made him want a poem at all is "dismissed as irrelevant." Stated, not smuggled.

## 2. The explanation in parts

In his words: settle the dénouement first; choose an **effect** before writing; **extent** — brief, one sitting, about a hundred lines (108); **province** — Beauty; **tone** — melancholy; **device** — the refrain, with its *application* varied; refrain brief, therefore one word; word sonorous, long *o* with *r* → "Nevermore"; speaker a non-reasoning creature that talks — parrot rejected, Raven on tone; **topic** — death of a beautiful woman, lips of a bereaved lover; queries graded up to a climax, the climax stanza written first to fix metre; verse — trochaic octameter, originality by combination; room, tempest, bird in by the window misheard as a tap; bust of Pallas; the fantastic entrance, then the drop to seriousness; two stanzas added last for an under-current; raven as emblem of Mournful and Never-ending Remembrance.

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | What holds it, or what is wrong |
|---|---|---|
| Dénouement first; start from the effect | Held if | rests on "air of consequence" — his own job, not tested |
| Extent ~100 lines, one sitting | Held if | job "unity of impression"; "psychal necessity" is asserted. The exact 108 is **loose** — 90 or 120 would do |
| Beauty as province | Borrowed | rests on an aesthetic theory tested nowhere here |
| Melancholy as tone | Borrowed | "all experience has shown" — a general claim, asserted |
| Refrain with varied application | Held | universality is checkable; the swap (no refrain) visibly breaks the poem |
| One-word refrain | Held at "brief"; Loose at "one word" | the variation job; two words would still vary, less easily |
| "Nevermore" | Loose | "Evermore" meets every condition he names. What really holds it — that it *denies*, so it answers a query — he never says. And "it was the very first which presented itself" is intuition offered where a reason is claimed |
| Raven over parrot | Held | a rejected swap; the ominous reputation is checkable |
| Death of a beautiful woman | Held if | the ranking is asserted; swap an old man's death, or a mother's |
| Graded queries; climax stanza first | Held | this one can be checked against the poem — the queries do rise |
| Chamber, tempest, tap at the door | Held | each names a job that could be seen failing; the tempest does two |
| Bust of Pallas | Held | contrast job plus the sound of "Pallas"; swap "Minerva" and the sound job fails |
| Two concluding stanzas | Held if | job "suggestiveness" is his requirement; the addition is disclosed plainly |
| Emblem of Remembrance | Held if | job "under-current"; the last-line reveal is checkable |

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** If "The Raven" had flopped, would he have told this story? Partly — the method can also predict failure (too long, wrong tone). But the example is chosen because it is "the most generally known." The demonstration is picked *on* its result.

**Direction.** He is working backwards from the finished poem and calling the reconstruction a production account. His evidence is memory, three years on. That is *recalled* provenance — fitted. It is held where the poem can check it, and nowhere else.

**The answer in the starting points.** "The effect" is chosen first, so of course every part serves it. This is the method's own trap: write the jobs, then the parts that do them. The jobs — Beauty, melancholy, popularity, suggestiveness — are Poe's own and untested. That is why so much above is *held if*.

**Pairs that pull.** Originality against the refrain and the confessed borrowed metre — he answers with "originality of combination," which needs a line drawn and isn't. "Supremeness at all points" against the plan to enfeeble rival stanzas — stated honestly. Popular taste against critical taste — claimed compatible, with no line given where they would part.

**Catch-alls.** "Originality" can absorb any choice; he polices it once, when he admits the metre isn't his. "The effect" can absorb any detail. A gauge would be one point he could not fit — he offers none.

**Where the parts came from: almost all asserted, then fitted to the finished poem.** He tells us why each thing is there, after the thing exists. Two parts are genuinely *built* — they commit to something untried: a long poem cannot hold unity of effect; a rival stanza, were it stronger, would be weakened on purpose. Those can be caught out. The rest cannot.

**Best rival.** A magazine writer working in a familiar gothic manner, using known props, who later writes a rationalist fable of his own process. Both accounts fit the finished poem identically. Nothing Poe says about tone, effect or Beauty pulls them apart — those are the shared, softer part. The separator is the one hard claim: he "first put pen to paper" on the climax stanza.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

Two moves. **(a)** Check the drafts: is the Lenore stanza's page earlier than the others, and is the metre settled on it first? **(b)** Give the effect-story a gauge — name one detail in the poem that does *not* serve the effect, and say so. Either would separate the rival accounts.

## 6. What this does not show

Hard to vary is not true. Even with every part held, the essay could be wrong about what was in Poe's head. And "Nevermore" being loose does not make it the wrong word. The poem is the poem.

## 7. One next step

Ask for the manuscripts, and look at dates and order. That single comparison tells the two rival accounts apart, and nothing else in the essay can.

**4. Whole-explanation checks**

- Flip: An account built to show that every choice served a successful effect. If "The Raven" had failed, would he have told the same story? Partly — the method can also predict failure (too long, wrong tone). But the *example* is picked because it is "the most generally known." The demonstration is selected on its result.

**5. What would make it harder to vary**
Two moves. (a) One deadline-free check against a checkable claim: the drafts — do they show the Lenore stanza written first, and the metre fixed before the earlier stanzas? (b) A gauge for the effect-story: name one detail in the poem that does *not* serve the effect, and say so. Either would cut both rivals down.

**6. What this does not show**
Hard to vary is not true. Even if every part were held, the essay could still be false about what was in Poe's head; and a loose part ("Nevermore") is not a wrong word — the poem is the poem.

Ask for the drafts. Look at whether the climax stanza's sheet is earlier, and whether the metre is settled on it before the earlier stanzas exist. That single comparison tells the two rival accounts apart — and nothing else in the essay can.
